reason: judged the change against the issue: 2 requirement(s) not met or not sure

unmet: PATH-1: The auto-resume via `latest` symlink entry path (ENTR-2) is never exercised; `resume-entry-points-test.sh` path 2 sets `ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$P2_STATE_FILE"` (line 219), which causes the symlink branch guard `[[ -z "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE:-}" && -L "$state_dir/latest" ]]` in runner.sh to be false — the new code at runner.sh:2205 is dead in the test. PATH-1 requires "each has its own test." — "Every way to resume (`--resume`, auto-resume on restart, and `zbuild pipeline resume --run-id`) finds the interrupted run's state in `runs/<run_id>/` and behaves as R1. Each has its own test."

GUAR-1: Fresh cycle runs now emit `stage.start` for every cycle member because `cycle_dispatch_stage` at runner.sh:3213 uses `if [[ "$_cd_iter" -gt 0 ]]` with no `_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE` check, and `_cd_iter` equals the iteration counter (always ≥ 1). The golden file shape-floor failures for `tests/golden/full-pipeline/event-sequence.golden` and `tests/golden/parity/event-sequence.golden` confirm the event sequence has changed for fresh runs. Additionally, the FRSH-1 assertion added in the DIFF to verify cycle-member dispatch on fresh runs is in a test that stubs out `cycle_dispatch_stage` (cycle-member-dispatch-events-test.sh line 67–85), so the new code is never called and the assertion (`expected: 2, got: 0`) cannot pass, leaving GUAR-1 unverified by any passing test. — "A run with no prior state behaves exactly as today. This is a guard."
